content:
maria: Heads-up — nightly canary started seeing a spike in OOMs after yesterday's reuse-policy change. Mostly on 16GB cards, tails during bursty batch windows.

maria: Quick excerpt from the GPU profiler: 
```text
[2026-03-17T21:04:12Z] GPU0 OOM alloc failed: 438MB (tensor_pool:sentinel_alloc)
peak_reserved: 14.8GB, total_reserved: 15.3GB, free: 128MB
slab_fragmentation_ratio: 0.42
logits_scratchpad_peak: 190MB
```

steven: Wait — we only flipped reuse_policy to "aggressive" in PR #482, we didn't touch sentinel sizing itself, right?

ashok: Correct, PR #482 enabled aggressive_reclaim and reduced slab compaction frequency to avoid compaction stalls. That combo can increase short-lived small-fragment churn; sentinel buffers are currently excluded from compaction which could leave them pinned.

jen: Alert: deploy-bot flagged canary rejection +3% on 16GB workers. Are we going to rollback? :thinking_face:

maria: Short-term mitigation proposal: change reuse_policy->compact-on-release (so sentinel candidates become compactable), lower tensor_pool.reserve_ratio to 0.06, and cap scratchpad workspace. Also enable eager_return for logits buffers so they don't sit in the pool between requests.

maria: Config snippet I'm going to test locally: 
```yaml
runtime:
  tensor_pool:
    reserve_ratio: 0.06          # reduce reserved margin to free more address space
    reuse_policy: compact-on-release
    eager_return: [logits, activations]
  scratchpad:
    max_workspace_bytes: 67108864  # 64MB cap on temporary workspace per request
```

steven: Sounds reasonable. Test plan: repro load on gpu-16-canary with the config, collect slab histograms + fragmentation, and verify per-gpu oom_rate < 1% before rolling. Ashok, can you run the repro?

ashok: Starting the rehearse run now (100k requests, mixed seq lengths, KV-heavy). Also instrumenting a new metric "sentinel_reserve_usage" to see how often sentinel blocks are preventing allocs.

perf-bot: Job canary-oom-repro-1977001245 queued and started by ashok.

ashok: Early numbers after 25k requests: OOMs dropped from 2.7% -> 0.5% with the reserve_ratio tweak. Fragmentation down ~18%. Still seeing a handful of large peaks when seq_len spikes hit long KV sequences.

maria: Good improvement. Next steps: roll config to 10% of canary cluster, enable automatic rollback if per-gpu oom_rate > 1% over 10m, and keep the sentinel_reserve_usage metric on dashboards. I'll open a short RFC for making "compact-on-release" the default when aggressive_reclaim is enabled.

jen: Please include SRE in the RFC and add the rollback trigger to the rollout plan. If the rollout causes customer impact we need a 15-minute playbook.

steven: Also let's add a micro-benchmark to the perf suite that exercises logits + KV churn so we catch this earlier in CI.

ashok: Will push the test and the metric in the next hour and post the raw slab hist results.

maria: Thanks — for context I'll paste the small debug allocator dump I'm saving to the thread: 
```text
ALLOC TRACE (short):
- request 12345: alloc activ 32MB -> got slab@0x7f.. (reused)
- request 12346: alloc logits 180MB -> created sentinel slab@0x8a.. (not compactable)
- request 12347: free activ 32MB -> returned to pool (marked reclaimable)
- request 12348: alloc activ 64MB -> fail: no contiguous chunk (fragmentation) -> OOM
```

maria: If we see this pattern again after rollout, priority is to: 1) enable eager_return for logits, 2) temporarily increase compaction frequency, 3) fall back to previous policy and roll back config.

perf-bot: Canary run completed: total=100000, oom_count=502, oom_rate=0.502% (post-tweak). Baseline run oom_rate=2.71%.

ashok: Uploading slab_hist.csv and profiler traces to /internal/snapshots/1977001234/ — will annotate key ranges.

maria: Nice work. I'll schedule the 10% canary and the rollback policy. Filing a short doc after rollout with timelines and the metric thresholds.

jen: Great — keep SRE on standby for the rollout window. :thumbsup:
